sample_unit: frontline neonatal health care workers (plus 3 key informant interviewees)
models_evaluated: ML-derived paper-based neonatal risk predictor tool

links.outcome: Reported documentation burden and workflow integration after ML risk tool implementation
links.effect: 40% (4/10) reported increased documentation burden during high patient volume; 80% (8/10) agreed the tool improves care prioritization within 48 hours.
links.quote: However, workflow integration was workload-sensitive: 40% (4/10) reported an increased documentation burden during periods of high patient volume.

unlisted_practices: Structured onboarding and administrative endorsement to support adoption of AI tools
Paper-based delivery of ML-derived risk predictor in low-resource settings

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world usability and workflow integration of an ML-derived paper-based neonatal risk prediction tool used by frontline clinicians in 3 Kenyan hospitals.
